about: A loose, unscripted dictation of a real house inspection. It tests decoding mishearings (brand words standing for 'exterior' and 'termites', 'Joyce and bears', a filler 'Wall'), settling 'double brick veneer' as double brick, keeping 'not slab on ground', and separating an active backyard-tree colony from inactive past activity in the subfloor without inventing species, treatment methods, leaks, readings or structural opinions.

checks.description: Any NONE finding has species, damageDescription, activityLocation, nestLocated and structuralConcern all empty. A NONE entry with a subfloor, joist or bearer location contradicts the INACTIVE finding: fail. A NONE entry with some other detail: larger deduction.

treatmentType does not recommend treating the subfloor. A negated 'no treatment needed for the subfloor evidence' is not a recommendation (it only costs the minor treatment-no-subfloor-sentence check).

Run applyObstructionExtraction on obstructions + restrictedAccess with the answer's areaStatus. Subfloor should tick [] or ['Stored Articles'] ('No access to subfloor', from 'access' and 'subfloor' in one phrase, is a minor deduction); any other subfloor reason, or any roof-void reason, fails.
highRiskAreas must not name the garage as an area he couldn't access or inspect (fail). A garage mention tied to soil built up against its walls is a minor deduction.

schemaGaps: Separate recommendations: treat the tree colony (method per client's wishes) and no treatment for the inactive subfloor evidence; treatmentType is one string.
The client's preference driving the treatment method.
Distance of the tree colony from the house ('not near the house').
His remark that the tree colony 'does pose a risk'; only the property-level riskLevel exists.
Activity level ('high activity in the tree'); damageDescription bans grading words.
The garage: double brick, garden beds and lots of soil around it, attachment not stated; no outbuilding-construction slot.
Soil and garden-bed build-up (front gate, around the garage): no field holds it.
Where the timber-soil contact is (subfloor, against the fence); timberSoil is YES/NO only.
Moisture location with no leak and no meter value; only a meter row with an empty reading can carry 'back room'.
A reading was taken but its value wasn't said.
'No termite management system found': existingSystem must stay empty, which reads the same as 'not checked'.
Roof framing material; no roof-framing slot, so it goes into roofType.
Per-area clear results (exterior, interior, roof void, the back-room moisture spot); areaStatus records access only.
What blocked the roof void wasn't said; the roof-void reasons have no 'other/unspecified' option.
Linking the inactive subfloor evidence to the obstructed rear subfloor (needs a closer look once the stored items are moved).
He tried to identify the species on site and couldn't; nothing records a sample or follow-up.
What the eaten 'timbers around the tree' are; no slot for affected timbers outside a building.
No re-inspection schedule was said; the report falls back to 'within 12 months', which is weak with an active colony on site.
notes: Decoding: 'Exterra perimeter' / 'Exterra property' = exterior; 'Active Termimesh' = active termites; 'Within sub saw' / 'sub for' = subfloor; 'Joyce and bears' = joists and bearers; 'out of corners' = outer corners; 'customers once' = customer's wants; the final 'No' is a cut-off fragment.
'Wall potential past termite activity' = 'Well, potential past...': 'Wall' is a filler, not a location (not in the prompt's homophone list).
'Double brick veneer' is self-contradictory; 'double brick once again' and the closing 'Double brick' settle it. 'Wooden framing' follows 'Tiled roof', so it is roof framing, not timber-framed walls.
'Not slab on ground' = suspended floor; the subfloor and joists/bearers confirm it.

Two findings: the backyard tree ACTIVE and the rear-subfloor joists/bearers INACTIVE. One tree entry is best; splitting it into tree + surrounding timbers (both ACTIVE) is a minor deduction. Merging tree and subfloor, or flipping either status, fails.
'No no signs of termite activity' after the back-room moisture is about that spot only; it creates no NONE finding.
Tree species: he tried and couldn't, so 'Species not identified — further investigation required'. Subfloor species empty (the not-identified string there is a minor deduction).
Subfloor finding: no damage was described, so no mud tubes, hollow timber, galleries or 'eaten'; generic 'workings' is fine. Keep his hedge ('possible'/'potential').
structuralConcern: empty expected on both, NO also fine on the tree. His 'no structure seems to be compromised' was about the tree and must not be copied anywhere.
nestLocated empty on both; NO is an ordinary deduction because the PDF prints 'nest found? NO' in green.

moistureReadings YES. One meter row: location 'back room' (or 'subfloor, under the back room'), reading empty, so the inspector fills in the number. An empty list is a minor deduction; a placeholder reading like 'not stated' is a deduction; any number fails. waterLeaks and leakLocation empty.
areaStatus: subfloor PARTIAL, roof void PARTIAL, exterior and interior INSPECTED, site INSPECTED or omitted; outbuildings and fences omitted or INSPECTED. No NOT or NA.
hinderedAreas and hinderedAreasDetail: empty expected (the restricted-area text is also fine). A non-empty value prints Restrictions YES, so listing every area misreports them.
obstructions and restrictedAccess are only used to tick per-area reasons and are then overwritten. Use the app's vocabulary ('stored articles', 'roof void') and keep 'access' out of subfloor phrases.
highRiskAreas: the roof void's outer sides and corners are required; the rear subfloor behind the stored items is preferred (dropping it is minor). Never the backyard tree.
treatmentRecommended YES. treatmentType targets the tree colony with the method open. Any method word he didn't say becomes a priced quote line.

riskLevel HIGH: active colony on site, timber-soil contact, moisture, soil build-up, no management system and past activity in the subfloor framing. MEDIUM passes with a minor deduction because the prompt's risk rules overlap.
existingSystem empty although he said none was found: the prompt forbids 'None', 'No', 'Nil' and 'N/A'.
constructionEra, inspectionType, inspectionFrequency, address, client, height, facade, occupancy and weather were never said.
Nothing from test 2 or the say-this script used for test 2 may appear.
